guideTitle: 6 Best Wireless TV Speakers for Bedrooms in 2026
metaTitle: Best Wireless TV Speakers for Bedrooms 2026
metaDescription: Six bedroom-friendly TV speakers and soundbars compared on width, height, bass control, connections and surround options for small rooms.
introParagraphs: A bedroom TV has different needs than a living room set. The room is small, bass can bounce off nearby walls and disturb neighbors, the TV may sit on a dresser, and the person watching is often in bed rather than centered on a sofa. That favors compact bars, bass controls and simple connections over big surround systems with five boxes to place.

This guide compares six distinct options: the Evinof compact RF speaker, the ULTIMEA 2.1ch bar that is 16 inches wide, the RIOWOIS 17 inch bar that is just over 2.5 inches tall, the TOVZAIX 100W detachable bar, the LG S40TR with wireless rear speakers and the ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch Dolby Atmos system for larger bedrooms. We evaluated each on listing specs and buyer feedback themes, with placement, bass control and connections weighted for small rooms.
Measure the shelf under your TV and the distance from the bed to the screen before you buy. A bar that is taller than the gap under the screen will block the picture.

products.name: ULTIMEA 2.1ch Soundbar with Built-in Subwoofer
products.description:
The ULTIMEA 2.1ch is a compact bar with built-in dual speakers, a 3-inch subwoofer and side-firing bass ports that deepen the low end and widen the sound. It lists 132W of peak power, a width of 16 inches and Bluetooth 5.4. The maker says it fits on a stand or cabinet, and an app with EQ controls and regular over-the-air updates tunes the sound.

In a small room this design avoids the boom of a separate floor subwoofer, and BassMX lets you adjust the bass level down for night viewing. The tradeoff is that built-in bass is shallower than a separate sub and the stereo image cannot imitate surround speakers, so movies sound wider but not enveloping.

In ownership terms there is a single bar to power and a single cable to the TV. It sits in the lower-middle price ranks. Compared with the RIOWOIS 17 inch bar, it adds a built-in sub and an app, and against the LG S40TR, it needs no rear speakers to place.
products.bestFor: Small bedrooms that want bass without a separate subwoofer.
pros: Built-in 3 inch subwoofer with side ports
App with EQ and over-the-air updates
cons: Peak power figure is not continuous output

products.name: RIOWOIS 17-Inch Sound Bar
products.description:
The RIOWOIS is a 17 inch bar that stands a little over 2.5 inches tall, with a bass reflex port and compatibility with the Fire TV remote. The listing describes it as compact enough to mount or place in most spaces, and its DSP offers three sound modes for movies, music and news. Its pitch is hearing every word of dialogue.

The low height is the notable point for bedrooms, where a dresser top or wall bracket leaves little room under the screen. The Fire TV remote compatibility means one remote for volume. The tradeoff is that the listing gives no wattage, no subwoofer and no connection list on the listing, so check the product page for ARC, optical and Bluetooth.

In ownership terms it has the second-lowest price rank here and fits almost anywhere. Compared with the ULTIMEA 2.1ch at 16 inches wide, it is slightly wider but has no built-in sub. Against the TOVZAIX, it is smaller and lists less.
products.bestFor: Dressers and shelves with very little clearance under the TV.
cons: No wattage or connections in the listing
Bass reflex port only, no subwoofer

products.name: TOVZAIX 100W Sound Bar for Smart TV
products.description:
The TOVZAIX is a 100W bar with Bluetooth 5.3 plus ARC, optical and AUX inputs, and a detachable 2-in-1 design that lets you use it as two units. It offers three EQ modes for movies, music and news. The listing positions it for TV shows, games and music.

The connection list is the draw for a bedroom, where TVs are often older or secondhand. Optical covers older sets and ARC handles newer ones, though optical cannot carry Dolby Atmos. The detachable design could let you split the bar, though you should check the product page for how, and the maker is less established.

In ownership terms there is one bar to place and one cable to run. It sits in the middle of the price ranks. Compared with the ULTIMEA 2.1ch, it has no built-in subwoofer claim, and against the Evinof it adds output and inputs.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms with older TVs that need several input options.
pros: Bluetooth 5.3, ARC, optical and AUX inputs
Movie, music and news EQ modes
cons: Detachable use needs checking on the page

products.name: Evinof 2.4G Wireless TV Speaker
products.description:
The Evinof is a small standalone speaker with a 2.4GHz link that the listing calls zero-latency and a TV mode with voice enhancement technology. A Bluetooth mode plays music from a phone, and the listed range is 100 feet. It is not a soundbar, so it suits a nightstand rather than a TV shelf.

For a bedroom it solves the late-night problem: a speaker near the bed lets you hear dialogue at a lower volume. The RF link avoids the 100 to 250 millisecond delay common to plain Bluetooth. The tradeoff is no bass or surround, and you should check which TV outputs the base accepts.

In ownership terms it takes almost no room. It sits in the upper-middle price ranks. Compared with the bars here, it is the only one built for dialogue near the listener, and against the soundbars it lacks a wide sound stage.
products.bestFor: A nightstand speaker for clearer dialogue at low volume.

products.name: LG S40TR 4.1ch Home Theater Soundbar

specList.label: Audio
specList.value: Dolby Audio with AI Sound Pro

products.description:
The LG S40TR is a 4.1 channel system with rear surround speakers and a wireless subwoofer, using Dolby Audio and an AI Sound Pro mode that adjusts to the content. The listing says the rear speakers connect wirelessly, so there is no long cable across the room. It aims to give a surround feel in rooms of different shapes.

Wireless parts still need power, so each rear speaker and the subwoofer needs an outlet, which is a real consideration in a bedroom. A subwoofer near a wall can boom in a small room, so check for a bass setting. It is the most expensive pick here, and the listing does not state Dolby Atmos.

In ownership terms it takes more space than the compact bars. Compared with the ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch, it has fewer channels and no Atmos claim, and against the ULTIMEA 2.1ch it adds real rear speakers.
products.bestFor: Larger bedrooms that want true rear surround speakers.
pros: Wireless subwoofer avoids an audio cable
Dolby Audio with AI Sound Pro
cons: Highest price rank of the six
Rear speakers and sub all need outlets

products.name: ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch Sound Bar with Dolby Atmos
products.description:
The ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch is a Dolby Atmos system with a bar, two surround speakers, up-firing speakers and a subwoofer. The up-firing drivers use neodymium magnets and 18-core voice coils for height effects, and SurroundX combines the rears and the Atmos drivers into a 360 degree sound field. The 5.1.2 label means five main channels, one subwoofer and two height channels.

Atmos height effects depend on an unobstructed ceiling and an HDMI ARC connection, so a bedroom with a sloped or cluttered ceiling may get little benefit. Many bedrooms are too small for this much hardware, and the extra power and speaker cables add clutter. It sits in the upper price ranks.

In ownership terms it is a project: place the bar, two rears and a sub. Compared with the LG S40TR, it adds Atmos height channels. Against the ULTIMEA 2.1ch, it is far larger and more complex.
products.bestFor: Large bedrooms or master suites with a clear ceiling and ARC TV.
cons: Atmos needs ARC and a clear ceiling

buyingCriteria.explanation: Measure the shelf and the gap under the screen. The RIOWOIS is a little over 2.5 inches tall and 17 inches wide, the ULTIMEA 2.1ch is 16 inches wide, and the rest need their dimensions checked on the product page. A bar taller than the clearance blocks the screen bottom. Wall mounting frees the dresser but needs the right hardware. If the TV sits on a dresser, leave a few inches of space behind the bar so the bass ports can breathe. A bar pushed against a wall can sound boomy even when it is small.

A large subwoofer near a wall can overpower a small room and disturb neighbors. The ULTIMEA 2.1ch uses a built-in 3 inch subwoofer with BassMX adjustment, the LG S40TR has a wireless subwoofer you must place sensibly and the ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch adds a larger sub. Look for a bass control and a night mode. Place subs away from corners. A useful rule is to start with the bass at its lowest setting and raise it until voices still sound clear, then stop. In apartments and shared walls, bass travels farther than treble, so a modest setting protects neighbors more than a low overall volume does.

HDMI ARC is the cleanest single cable and the minimum for Atmos, while optical carries Dolby Digital 5.1 but not Atmos. The TOVZAIX lists Bluetooth 5.3, ARC, optical and AUX, and the Evinof uses an RF link that often takes optical or 3.5mm. Check your TV's ports first. Older bedroom TVs often have optical only. The ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch needs ARC for Atmos, and the LG S40TR listing should be checked for its inputs, so a bedroom TV without ARC deserves a closer look at the product pages.

More channels do not always help in small rooms, where a 2.0 or 2.1 bar often fits better than a multi-channel system. The LG S40TR is 4.1 with real rear speakers, the ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch adds height channels, and the TOVZAIX is a single bar. Confirm whether rear speakers are real units or virtual. Rooms under about 15 square meters suit simple bars. Bedrooms with a bed between the TV and the back wall make rear speaker placement awkward, which is the practical argument against the LG S40TR and the ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch in a small room.

Bedroom viewing often means low volume, so voice clarity matters. The Evinof has a TV voice mode, the RIOWOIS and TOVZAIX offer news presets, and the ULTIMEA models list voice processing. A news or voice mode lifts the 1 to 4 kHz speech range. Low-lag links keep voices synced. If you watch in bed, set the voice mode first and leave music modes for the daytime. The Evinof's 100 feet of listed range also means a family member can move it without rewiring.

Wireless rear speakers and subwoofers remove the audio cable, not the power cable. The LG S40TR needs outlets for each rear and the sub, and the ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch needs space for all parts. Compact bars like the ULTIMEA 2.1ch and RIOWOIS need one plug. Count outlets near the TV before you buy. For a nightstand setup, the Evinof avoids soundbar cabling altogether, though its base unit still needs a connection to the TV.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and placement
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the 16 inch ULTIMEA 2.1ch, the 17 inch RIOWOIS at a little over 2.5 inches tall and the larger systems. Dimensions not stated were flagged. Bedroom fit was weighed heavily. The ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch and LG S40TR do not list a single footprint because they are multi-piece systems, so we judged them on how many parts need floor or shelf space.

howWeEvaluated.title: Bass and room fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at built-in versus separate subwoofers and bass controls, such as BassMX on the ULTIMEA 2.1ch. Small rooms penalize boomy setups. Output wattage claims such as 132W peak and 100W were not treated as equivalent. The LG S40TR and ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch carry separate subwoofers, so they were judged on bass control access rather than built-in bass.

howWeEvaluated.title: Connections
howWeEvaluated.description: We read the TOVZAIX input list, the Evinof RF link and the ARC need for Atmos on the ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch. Missing connection details were flagged. Older bedroom TVs were considered. The TOVZAIX led on input count, the LG on wireless rears and the ULTIMEA 2.1ch on Bluetooth 5.4.

howWeEvaluated.title: Dialogue features
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the Evinof voice mode with the news presets on the RIOWOIS and TOVZAIX and voice processing on the ULTIMEA models. Maker claims only. The RIOWOIS listing leans on hearing every word, but gives no technical detail, so it earned only modest credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The ULTIMEA 2.1ch leads on compact bass, the RIOWOIS on low profile, the TOVZAIX on inputs, the Evinof on near-bed dialogue, the LG on wireless rears and the ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch on Atmos. Scores come from specs and buyer feedback, not hands-on measurement.

howToChoose.intro: Two ways to fill a bedroom.

cards.label: Compact bar
cards.text: A single bar needs one cable and one outlet. The ULTIMEA 2.1ch, RIOWOIS and TOVZAIX fall here. Pick it for small rooms and simple setups. The ULTIMEA 2.1ch adds Bluetooth 5.4 and the TOVZAIX adds Bluetooth 5.3, so both pair with a phone for bedtime music as well.

cards.label: Surround system
cards.text: Rear speakers and a sub add immersion but add clutter. The LG S40TR and ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch fall here. Pick it for larger rooms where you can place rears. Rear speakers need cables or power at the back of the bed, and Atmos height effects need a clear ceiling, so measure before committing.

faq.q: Which bar fits a small dresser?
faq.a: The RIOWOIS stands a little over 2.5 inches tall and is 17 inches wide, and the ULTIMEA 2.1ch is 16 inches wide. Measure the clearance under your screen first. Check the product page for the dimensions of the TOVZAIX, which the listing does not give.

It can, especially against shared walls, because bass travels through structures. The ULTIMEA 2.1ch has a built-in sub with adjustable bass, so you can turn it down at night. Keep separate subs away from corners and shared walls.

faq.q: Do wireless rear speakers need power?
faq.a: Yes. The LG S40TR rear speakers connect wirelessly, but wireless only removes the audio cable, not the power cable. Plan outlets for each rear speaker and the subwoofer before you order.

faq.q: Is Dolby Atmos worth it in a bedroom?
faq.a: Only with a clear ceiling and an ARC-capable TV. The ULTIMEA 5.1.2ch uses up-firing drivers and needs space for rear speakers and a subwoofer. Most small bedrooms are better served by a compact bar.

faq.q: What if my bedroom TV only has optical?
faq.a: The TOVZAIX lists optical along with ARC and AUX, so it can work with an older set. Optical carries Dolby Digital 5.1 but not Atmos. Check your TV ports before choosing a system that expects ARC.
No. It is a small speaker with a 2.4GHz RF link and a TV voice mode. It suits a nightstand and clearer dialogue at low volume, but it will not give a wide stereo stage or deep bass.

faq.q: Can I mount these on the wall?
faq.a: The RIOWOIS listing describes it as compact enough to mount, and the ULTIMEA 2.1ch fits a stand or cabinet per its listing. Check each product page for mounting hardware and weight. Do not mount anything above the bed unless it is rated for it.
